topic: Current news/lifestyle topic: whether small ("mini" or "micro") handbags are genuinely gaining renewed attention in fashion right now, as a light, consumer/lifestyle-oriented story (not hard news such as AI, space security, or policy). Research this without assuming the conclusion that 'tiny bags are back' — actively check for and report evidence on any of the following possible realities: (a) mini/micro bags are genuinely regaining visibility in recent runway shows, retail, or styling coverage; (b) large and oversized bags remain equally or more prominent at the same time (a polarization between very small and very large, rather than a single trend); (c) any renewed attention is concentrated in specific brands or runway moments rather than being a broad, general shift; (d) any attention is driven mainly by a small number of celebrity styling moments rather than a broader industry or retail pattern. Prioritize credible fashion publications and trade/retail sources (Vogue, ELLE, Harper's Bazaar, Marie Claire, other major fashion publications, Fashion Week runway coverage, and credible retail or trend-forecasting sources) over generic entertainment/gossip sites. Specific brand or celebrity examples may be cited as illustrations, but do not center the coverage on celebrity gossip. Also look for any credible reporting connecting small-bag attention to practical factors such as accessory-first styling (bag as accessory rather than functional carry-all), minimalism/decluttering behavior, or any other credible driver — but only report a causal or explanatory link if it is actually stated or supported by a credible source, not as an assumption. Avoid overgeneralizations such as claims that 'everyone' is using tiny bags, do not treat a single celebrity's styling choice as proof of a broad trend, avoid product-catalog-style listing of specific items/prices, avoid unsupported generational claims (e.g. about 'Gen Z') unless directly supported by a cited source, and avoid unsupported economic-anxiety-style causal explanations for the trend. If the evidence for a broad 'tiny bags are back' narrative turns out to be weak, ambiguous, or limited to a narrow runway/celebrity phenomenon, report that limitation directly rather than asserting a general trend.
